title: Code Splitting and Dynamic Reducers
description: Reduce initial bundle size and load reducers on demand with dynamic imports and store injection.

data.text: Large apps ship a single Redux store with **every reducer** loaded up front. That means a `settings` reducer and its dependencies load even if the user never opens the settings page. **Code splitting** fixes this by loading reducers only when their feature is needed.

data.title: What we are splitting
data.text: We split two things: the React code for a feature (with `React.lazy`), and the Redux slice/reducer for that feature (with dynamic `injectReducer`).

data.title: Static reducer (the old way)
data.content: Every reducer is in the initial bundle

data.text: Above, the user pays the cost of all three reducers on the very first page load — even if they only ever visit `/login`.

The idea: build a `combineReducers` that supports being mutated at runtime. When a feature route mounts, it asks the store to **inject** its reducer under a chosen key. From that point on, the reducer is part of the store.

data.text: Before `React.lazy`, libraries like `react-loadable` and `@loadable/component` handled the same job. They still work and add features like SSR-friendly placeholders.

data.title: Loadable Components
Don't double-register
data.text: Always check whether the reducer key already exists before injecting. Calling `injectReducer` twice with the same key resets state and re-runs initial effects.

terms.definition: Breaking your bundle into smaller chunks that load on demand.
`import('./module.js')` returns a promise and creates a separate chunk in the bundle.

Store method that swaps in a new root reducer at runtime.

items: Server-side rendering: defer injection until after hydration
Tests: reset the store between tests so injected reducers don't leak
Selectors: ensure they're defined **after** the reducer is injected
Don't inject in render — wrap in `useEffect` or route guards

data.title: Split the dashboard feature
data.description:
Take a monolithic store with `auth`, `todos`, `dashboard`. Move `dashboard` into its own lazy chunk.
1. Create a `useInjectReducer` hook.
2. Wrap the `/dashboard` route with `React.lazy` and `Suspense`.
3. Verify in the Network tab that `dashboard.js` only loads when you visit `/dashboard`.
steps: Use `React.lazy` for the component AND `import('./dashboardSlice')` for the reducer.
Test that navigating away and back does **not** re-inject the reducer.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Dynamic reducers let you load slices on demand instead of up front
`React.lazy` handles UI; a custom `injectReducer` handles state
`replaceReducer` is the API that swaps in new reducers at runtime
Watch for double-injection and SSR pitfalls
Measure bundle size before and after with `webpack-bundle-analyzer`
data.takeaway: Code splitting shrinks initial bundles and speeds up large apps.
